failure_summary: OI-203, now 5/5 deterministic: the better move col5 ENDS the game (2345153551111014334 is [GAME OVER], completing c3r1·c4r2·c5r3·c6r4) yet render_decision.link.text (L1) calls it "completes your threat to make four next move at c5r3" and the afterBest board is rendered shown:true with six live major/double entries and no game-over statement, so all five runs teach a threat to be cashed later ("keeps that threat alive", run 4 "creates the threat to finish it next turn") instead of "you had four-in-a-row available right now" — A7d fail on every run; secondaries OI-194 (that same L1 text embeds raw c5r3, echoed into player prose on runs 0/1/3 → A5a+G1) and OI-202 (reading key inversion, run 0 "they get the tougher defense" while replyHistogram is afterBest 0 / afterPlayed 1).
notes:
Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 null (not scored). A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_subset_2026-08-26T15-47-56Z_mechanical.json (all pass, all 5 keys present). Model gpt-5.4-mini = PRODUCTION-FIDELITY run, so prompt_confusion could not be separated from model capability; the decisive attribution here is model-INDEPENDENT (the frame text and the terminal board are wrong before any model reads them). Step 0b done: PROMPT built via buildReasonRenderModel+assembleGroundedPrompt — it contains the L1 sentence with raw "c5r3" verbatim and contains no statement that afterBest is terminal, confirming the leak/omission is render-side. Boards observed with ./visualize_board.sh: decision 234515355111101433 shows <X> gravity-top major at col5 row3, scr col5=+12 col7=-2; afterBest 2345153551111014334 = [GAME OVER]; afterPlayed 2345153551111014336 keeps <X> at col5row3 and the opponent takes it (render_decision.finalMovestring 23451535511110143364, ply 20 col 4).
A7d (all 5 runs): every run defers a game-ending move to a later turn — run 0 'keep your threat ... alive', run 1 'it builds your threat to make four next move', run 2 'keeps that threat alive ... shut off your next-move four', run 3 'kept your threat ... alive', run 4 'creates the threat to finish it next turn'. The transferable idea taught is wrong: afterBest is terminal. Attribution OI-203 (render_bug), not model failure.
A5a (runs 0,1,3): raw cNrM notation in player-facing prose — run 0 'the square at c5r3' plus 'c3r1, c4r2, c5r3, and c6r4', runs 1 and 3 'c5r3'. The assembled prompt says 'Never write a raw square' while L1 hands the model 'at c5r3' twice. OI-194, render_bug. Runs 2 and 4 avoided raw cells and pass A5.
G1 (runs 0,1,3): same leak — the answer violates the rendered artifact's own explicit rule about raw squares.
A4 (run 0): 'so they get the tougher defense' is false against the render's own numbers — READING_KEY says fewer replies = tougher defense, and the rendered replyHistogram is afterBest 0 / afterPlayed 1, i.e. the blunder left them MORE ways, and afterBest 0 means they cannot hold at all. OI-202, render_bug. Run 1 A4 passes: opponent taking c5r3 and 'column 7' are both board-true.
G5 (runs 0,1): the afterBest tactics list carries six live major/double entries on a position that is already won ([GAME OVER]); a terminal board has no threats in the sense the list means. Also on the decision board, 'double at c3r3 (opp, window c3r3·c7r4)' labels two separate non-gravity opponent majors as a single fork square (the opp-double alias role says 'the single fork square' but its spec is a two-cell windows: list) — OI-204 shape.
G7 (runs 2,4): membership passed mechanically and annotationRepairs is empty on all 5 runs, but both runs bind [zone:c5r3] (spec form of the required you-immediate, role 'the single square where you can make four next move') to the words 'column 5' — column words on a single-square handle, the exact shape mismatch the prompt's MATCH THE SHAPE block forbids, and better-col was offered for exactly those words. prompt_confusion, minor. Runs 0,1,3 bind square words to the square handle and line words to the line handle correctly. Note all runs emit zone SPECS ('c5r3', 'windows:...', 'col7') rather than the offered HANDLE names; the pipeline accepted them (annotationRepairs empty) so this is not scored as a G7 membership failure.
G6 pass: L1 is the right route for realized_denied/missed_own; patternOnAfterBestBoard null is defensible on a terminal board, though the render simultaneously offers you-double/you-major aliases on that same afterBest board — an internal inconsistency worth folding into OI-203.
G3 pass: afterPlayed (shown:false, tag-set identical) was not needed; the opponent's occupation of c5r3 is legible on the decision board.
OI-183 caveat: the harness calls the model once, so no retry ran — but no run here omitted a required handle, so the deterministic A7d failure is not a retry artifact.
